title: What can you say about saffron in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library gives no supported wording for saffron, because no listed source supports one at a dose. Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Treats depression or anxiety".

wordings_to_avoid.why: Names mental health disorders; no listed source supports mood wording for saffron.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: A natural antidepressant, or works like Prozac
wordings_to_avoid.why: Compares the product to a drug. FDA's 2000 rule (page 1027) cites 'Herbal Prozac' as wording that ties a product to an approved drug.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Treats macular degeneration or other eye disease
wordings_to_avoid.why: Names a disease; no listed source supports it.

evidence_gap: None of the four listed sources gives a use or a dose for saffron. Health Canada's monograph list (checked 2026-10-15) has no saffron or Crocus sativus monograph, and saffron is not an ingredient of its antioxidants or cognitive function products monographs. ODS's fact-sheet index (Internet Archive copy of 2026-10-12) lists no saffron fact sheet. Regulation (EU) No 432/2012 lists no saffron claim, and FDA's lists show no health claim for it. EFSA's opinions were not read.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
